535	    def explain_dependencies(self, version, checklist, dependencies):
536	        # Read-only release-blocker explanation layered on check_dependencies:
537	        # the same validation, effective statuses and readiness rule, but the
538	        # report lists only the unfinished items that block required items,
539	        # each with the affected required items and their dependency paths.
540	        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
541	            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
542	        items = self._validated_checklist(checklist, version)
543	        prerequisites = self._validated_dependencies(dependencies, {item["id"] for item in items})
544	        # The whole store is validated before the version is looked up; a
545	        # missing store is treated as empty and then reports it as unknown.
546	        records = self._read_store()
547	        if version not in records:
548	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
549	        status_by_id = {item["id"]: item["status"] for item in items}
550	        effective = {}
551	
552	        def effective_status(item_id):
553	            # The same memoized effective status as check_dependencies.
554	            if item_id not in effective:
555	                status = status_by_id[item_id]
556	                if any(effective_status(prerequisite) != "done"
557	                       for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(item_id, ())):
558	                    status = "blocked"
559	                effective[item_id] = status
560	            return effective[item_id]
561	
562	        position = {item["id"]: index for index, item in enumerate(items)}
563	
564	        def best_paths(source):
565	            # Fewest-edge paths from source over the subgraph of items that
566	            # are not effectively done; equal-length paths are ordered by the
567	            # checklist positions of their nodes, first differing position
568	            # wins, so the dependency-array order never matters.
569	            costs = {source: (0, (position[source],))}
570	            paths = {source: [source]}
571	            heap = [((0, (position[source],)), source)]
572	            while heap:
573	                cost, node = heapq.heappop(heap)
574	                if cost != costs[node]:
575	                    continue
576	                for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(node, ()):
577	                    if effective_status(prerequisite) == "done":
578	                        continue
579	                    candidate = (cost[0] + 1, cost[1] + (position[prerequisite],))
580	                    if prerequisite not in costs or candidate < costs[prerequisite]:
581	                        costs[prerequisite] = candidate
582	                        paths[prerequisite] = paths[node] + [prerequisite]
583	                        heapq.heappush(heap, (candidate, prerequisite))
584	            return paths
585	
586	        # Trace from every required item that is not effectively done,
587	        # following only prerequisites that are themselves not effectively
588	        # done. Nodes declared pending or blocked count as reasons and their
589	        # own prerequisites are still traced; declared-done nodes only carry
590	        # the path. Optional items no required item reaches never appear.
591	        reason_requireds = {}
592	        paths_from = {}
593	        for item in items:
594	            if not item["required"] or effective_status(item["id"]) == "done":
595	                continue
596	            paths = best_paths(item["id"])
597	            paths_from[item["id"]] = paths
598	            for node in paths:
599	                if status_by_id[node] != "done":
600	                    reason_requireds.setdefault(node, set()).add(item["id"])
601	        ready = all(effective_status(item["id"]) == "done"
602	                    for item in items if item["required"])
603	        reasons = []
604	        for item in items:
605	            item_id = item["id"]
606	            if item_id not in reason_requireds:
607	                continue
608	            affected = [{"id": required_id, "path": paths_from[required_id][item_id]}
609	                        for required_id in (entry["id"] for entry in items if entry["required"])
610	                        if required_id in reason_requireds[item_id]]
611	            reasons.append({"id": item_id, "text": item["text"],
612	                            "required": item["required"], "status": item["status"],
613	                            "affected": affected})
614	        return {"version": version, "ready": ready, "reasons": reasons}

616	    def plan_dependencies(self, version, checklist, dependencies):
617	        # Read-only release preparation order plan layered on
618	        # check_dependencies: the same validation and readiness rule, but the
619	        # report batches the unfinished work still required for release. The
620	        # planning scope is every required item together with all of its direct
621	        # and indirect prerequisites, traversing declared-done nodes; only
622	        # items declared pending or blocked inside that scope are scheduled.
623	        # Nothing is written and the passed objects are never mutated.
624	        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
625	            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
626	        items = self._validated_checklist(checklist, version)
627	        prerequisites = self._validated_dependencies(dependencies, {item["id"] for item in items})
628	        # The whole store is validated before the version is looked up; a
629	        # missing store is treated as empty and then reports it as unknown.
630	        records = self._read_store()
631	        if version not in records:
632	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
633	        status_by_id = {item["id"]: item["status"] for item in items}
634	        effective = {}
635	
636	        def effective_status(item_id):
637	            # The same memoized effective status as check_dependencies.
638	            if item_id not in effective:
639	                status = status_by_id[item_id]
640	                if any(effective_status(prerequisite) != "done"
641	                       for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(item_id, ())):
642	                    status = "blocked"
643	                effective[item_id] = status
644	            return effective[item_id]
645	
646	        # Mark the planning scope: every required item plus every item reached
647	        # by following prerequisites from a required item. Edges out of
648	        # declared-done nodes are followed too, so an unfinished prerequisite
649	        # behind a done chain stays in scope; an optional branch no required
650	        # item reaches never enters the plan.
651	        scope = set()
652	
653	        def mark_scope(node):
654	            if node in scope:
655	                return
656	            scope.add(node)
657	            for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(node, ()):
658	                mark_scope(prerequisite)
659	
660	        for item in items:
661	            if item["required"]:
662	                mark_scope(item["id"])
663	        ready = all(effective_status(item["id"]) == "done"
664	                    for item in items if item["required"])
665	        # Reduce the prerequisite edges past declared-done nodes: an item's
666	        # effective unfinished prerequisites are its direct unfinished
667	        # prerequisites plus the unfinished prerequisites of any done direct
668	        # prerequisite, recursively. The indirect relation through a done
669	        # node therefore still orders the plan, while the done node itself is
670	        # never scheduled. Every reached prerequisite lies in scope because
671	        # mark_scope followed the same edges.
672	        reduced = {}
673	
674	        def unfinished_prerequisites(node):
675	            if node not in reduced:
676	                closure = set()
677	                for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(node, ()):
678	                    if status_by_id[prerequisite] == "done":
679	                        closure.update(unfinished_prerequisites(prerequisite))
680	                    else:
681	                        closure.add(prerequisite)
682	                reduced[node] = closure
683	            return reduced[node]
684	
685	        # Batch the unfinished scope items: each wave takes every not-yet-
686	        # scheduled item whose effective unfinished prerequisites are all in
687	        # earlier waves. The validated acyclic graph guarantees progress, so
688	        # the waves stay compact (no empty batch) and end with the pool empty.
689	        remaining = {item["id"] for item in items
690	                     if item["id"] in scope and status_by_id[item["id"]] != "done"}
691	        scheduled = set()
692	        waves = []
693	        while remaining:
694	            current = []
695	            for item in items:
696	                item_id = item["id"]
697	                if item_id in remaining and unfinished_prerequisites(item_id) <= scheduled:
698	                    current.append(item_id)
699	            scheduled.update(current)
700	            remaining.difference_update(current)
701	            waves.append(current)
702	        # blocked lists scope items declared blocked in checklist order,
703	        # independently of the waves; being planned never clears the block.
704	        blocked = [item["id"] for item in items
705	                   if item["id"] in scope and status_by_id[item["id"]] == "blocked"]
706	        return {"version": version, "ready": ready,
707	                "waves": waves, "blocked": blocked}

709	    @staticmethod
710	    def _validated_dependencies(dependencies, known_ids):
711	        # Validate the dependency map: an object mapping normalized item ids
712	        # to arrays of normalized prerequisite ids, each following the
713	        # checklist single-line id rule. Keys, array entries, unknown ends,
714	        # self dependencies and cycles are all rejected; empty maps and empty
715	        # arrays mean "no prerequisites".
716	        if not isinstance(dependencies, dict):
717	            raise ValueError("dependencies must be a JSON object")
718	        normalized = {}
719	        seen_keys = set()
720	        for item_id, prerequisites in dependencies.items():
721	            if not isinstance(item_id, str) or not item_id.strip() or "\n" in item_id or "\r" in item_id:
722	                raise ValueError("dependency item id must be a non-empty single-line string")
723	            item_id = item_id.strip()
724	            # Case-sensitive, no trimming beyond the ends, no Unicode normalization.
725	            if item_id in seen_keys:
726	                raise ValueError("dependency item id must be unique")
727	            seen_keys.add(item_id)
728	            if not isinstance(prerequisites, list):
729	                raise ValueError("dependency prerequisites must be arrays of item ids")
730	            ordered, seen = [], set()
731	            for prerequisite in prerequisites:
732	                if (not isinstance(prerequisite, str) or not prerequisite.strip()
733	                        or "\n" in prerequisite or "\r" in prerequisite):
734	                    raise ValueError("dependency item id must be a non-empty single-line string")
735	                prerequisite = prerequisite.strip()
736	                # Case-sensitive, no trimming beyond the ends, no Unicode normalization.
737	                if prerequisite in seen:
738	                    raise ValueError("dependency prerequisite ids must be unique within one item")
739	                seen.add(prerequisite)
740	                ordered.append(prerequisite)
741	            normalized[item_id] = ordered
742	        for item_id, prerequisites in normalized.items():
743	            if item_id not in known_ids:
744	                raise ValueError("dependency item id must exist in the checklist")
745	            for prerequisite in prerequisites:
746	                if prerequisite not in known_ids:
747	                    raise ValueError("dependency prerequisite id must exist in the checklist")
748	                if prerequisite == item_id:
749	                    raise ValueError("dependencies must not contain a self dependency")
750	        # Reject every remaining cycle, including cycles over optional items:
751	        # resolve every id with an empty trail set.
752	        visiting = set()
753	        settled = set()
754	
755	        def visit(node):
756	            if node in settled:
757	                return
758	            if node in visiting:
759	                raise ValueError("dependencies must not contain a cycle")
760	            visiting.add(node)
761	            for prerequisite in normalized.get(node, ()):
762	                visit(prerequisite)
763	            visiting.remove(node)
764	            settled.add(node)
765	
766	        for item_id in normalized:
767	            visit(item_id)
768	        return normalized

783	    def generate_checklist_with_dependencies(self, version, payload, dependencies):
784	        # Read-only dependency-aware checklist generation: the template is
785	        # filtered by the release's change categories exactly like
786	        # generate_checklist, then every direct and indirect prerequisite of
787	        # the selected items is added even when its own categories do not
788	        # apply. The whole dependency graph is validated against the whole
789	        # template first, so edges of template items the filter would drop
790	        # still have to be legal and acyclic. Nothing is written and the
791	        # passed objects are never mutated.
792	        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
793	            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
794	        items = self._validated_template(payload)
795	        # Every id in the dependency map, at either end, must reference a
796	        # template item: the complete map and the complete template are
797	        # validated, including items the category filter never selects.
798	        prerequisites = self._validated_dependencies(
799	            dependencies, {item["id"] for item in items})
800	        # The whole store is validated before the version is looked up.
801	        records = self._read_store()
802	        if version not in records:
803	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
804	        selected = self._applicable_template_items(items, records[version])
805	        selected_ids = {item["id"] for item in selected}
806	        # Close over every direct and indirect prerequisite of the selected
807	        # items; shared prerequisites are collected once. Only the member set
808	        # matters here: the final order always follows the template.
809	        closure = set(selected_ids)
810	        pending = list(selected_ids)
811	        while pending:
812	            node = pending.pop()
813	            for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(node, ()):
814	                if prerequisite not in closure:
815	                    closure.add(prerequisite)
816	                    pending.append(prerequisite)
817	        selected_by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in selected}
818	        # Final items keep template order: initially selected items stay in
819	        # their positions and prerequisites added solely for the closure slot
820	        # in at their template positions, even when their categories do not
821	        # apply. The selected dicts already carry the uniform pending item
822	        # shape; added prerequisites are rendered from their template entry.
823	        result_items, dependency_pairs = [], []
824	        for item in items:
825	            item_id = item["id"]
826	            if item_id not in closure:
827	                continue
828	            if item_id in selected_ids:
829	                result_items.append(dict(selected_by_id[item_id]))
830	            else:
831	                result_items.append({"id": item_id, "text": item["text"],
832	                                     "required": item["required"], "status": "pending"})
833	            # Every final id gets a normalized array in template order;
834	            # omitted items and declared empty arrays both freeze to [].
835	            dependency_pairs.append((item_id, list(prerequisites.get(item_id, ()))))
836	        # includedPrerequisites lists, in template order, only the items
837	        # added solely because of a dependency edge.
838	        included_prerequisites = [item["id"] for item in items
839	                                  if item["id"] in closure and item["id"] not in selected_ids]
840	        return {"version": version, "items": result_items,
841	                "dependencies": dict(dependency_pairs),
842	                "includedPrerequisites": included_prerequisites}

879	            if actual is None:

969	    def _audit_dependency_report(version, items, expected_items, prerequisites, closure):
970	        # Dependency report over the final expected set: actual checklist items
971	        # first in checklist order, then expected items absent from the
972	        # checklist in template order. Actual items keep their definition and
973	        # declared status; appended items take the template definition with a
974	        # pending status. Only dependency edges whose both ends lie in the final
975	        # set count; actual items outside it behave as having no prerequisites.
976	        actual_by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in items}
977	        missing_expected = [expected for expected in expected_items
978	                            if expected["id"] not in actual_by_id]
979	
980	        def declared_status(node):
981	            actual = actual_by_id.get(node)
982	            return actual["status"] if actual is not None else "pending"
983	
984	        effective = {}
985

1	# Release Desk
2	
3	Maintain local release records and generate Markdown notes grouped as Added, Changed and Fixed. Requires Python 3.10+; only the standard library is used.
4	
5	`python3 release_desk.py notes 1.1.0` renders the included second release. `python3 release_desk.py versions` lists sample versions in numeric order. `samples/next-changes.json` is a candidate change list; to try registration without changing the sample store, use `python3 release_desk.py --store .state/releases.json add 1.2.0 samples/next-changes.json` and query that same store.
6	
7	Version identifiers have exactly three nonnegative numeric components, without prefixes, prerelease suffixes or leading zeros. Each release has at least one single-line change with a recognized category. Existing versions cannot be replaced. Category order is fixed and the input order within a category is retained. This version does not inspect Git or publish packages.
8	
9	`python3 release_desk.py diff 1.0.0 1.1.0` compares two registered versions in the same store and prints a single-line JSON object with `baseVersion`, `targetVersion` and the `added`, `removed` and `unchanged` entries of the target relative to the base. Entries match on category plus trimmed, case-sensitive text; duplicates pair up by occurrence. Comparing a version with itself or a higher with a lower version is allowed. The comparison is read-only and never infers actual product changes.
10	
11	`ReleaseDesk.diff_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config)` is a read-only structural comparison of two externally supplied JSON configuration objects, and `python3 release_desk.py diff-config 1.0.0 1.1.0 base.json target.json` reads both configurations from UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); comparing a version with itself or a higher with a lower version is allowed. The configurations come solely from the arguments or files — they are never written to the store and never inferred from change entries — and neither the passed objects, the files nor the store are modified, and no directory is created.
12	
13	Each root configuration must be a JSON object. When the same field exists in both and both values are objects, comparison descends recursively; otherwise the complete values are compared. Arrays are never split: they compare as whole values and element order is significant, with objects inside arrays following the same object rules. A field or whole subobject present only in the target yields one `added` entry, one present only in the base yields one `removed` entry, both carrying `path` and `value`; a field present on both sides with differing values yields a `changed` entry carrying `path`, `before` (the base value) and `after` (the target value). All three arrays are always present, and identical configurations return three empty arrays. `path` is a JSON Pointer rooted at the empty string (`/a/b`, `/` for an empty field name), with `~` and `/` in field names escaped as `~0` and `~1`. Each array is sorted by path in Unicode code point order; key matching is case-sensitive with no Unicode normalization and empty key names are allowed. Booleans differ from numbers even when comparing `true` with `1`, numerically equal integers and floats compare equal, `null` differs from a missing field, and object key order is ignored.
14	
15	An invalid or unknown version, invalid store content, a non-object root, a non-string key, a non-JSON value (including non-finite numbers) or a circular reference raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects encoding errors, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level (the same whole-file duplicate-key rule as everywhere), printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2 for any of these and the single-line result with exit 0 on success. A missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown.
16	
17	`ReleaseDesk.preview_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config)` is a read-only three-way preview that checks whether applying the base→target plan would overwrite independent edits already present in the current configuration, and `python3 release_desk.py preview-config 1.0.0 2.0.0 base.json target.json current.json` reads all three configurations from UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed, just like `diff-config`. The configurations come solely from the arguments or files and follow the same validation, equality, pointer and key rules as `diff_config`, and nothing — the passed objects, the files, the store — is modified and no directory is created.
18	
19	For each field, the plan is the base→target change. A field the plan does not change keeps its current presence state and value, including independent current edits and current-only fields. When the plan does change a field, a current value equal to the target is kept, a current state equal to the base adopts the target (whole additions and deletions included), and any other state is resolved field by field only when the field exists on all three sides and all three values are objects; otherwise it is one conflict at that path whose preview keeps the current field's presence state and value. Whole subobject additions and deletions, arrays (never split) and type changes are always judged as a whole, so a whole-value conflict never lists subpaths; every other non-conflicting change still enters the preview. Equality uses the `diff_config` rules, including `null` differing from a missing field and two missing fields being equal. The result holds only `baseVersion`, `targetVersion`, `canApply`, `config` and `conflicts`: `config` is the complete previewed object, `canApply` is true only when `conflicts` is empty, and each conflict holds only `path` plus `base`, `target` and `current`, each of those holding a `present` boolean and a `value` only when present. `path` uses the same JSON Pointer escaping as `diff-config`, and `conflicts` is sorted by path in Unicode code point order. For example, a target that changes the port while the current config only changes a timeout keeps both changes, while both sides changing the same port to different values keeps the current port and reports a `/port` conflict.
20	
21	An invalid or unknown version, invalid store or a configuration violating the existing config validation rules raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects encoding errors, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the three files, printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid preview prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when it reports conflicts, and a missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown. Neither success nor failure modifies the arguments, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory.
22	
23	`ReleaseDesk.resolve_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config, decisions)` is a read-only confirmation layer over `preview_config`, and `python3 release_desk.py resolve-config 1.0.0 2.0.0 base.json target.json current.json decisions.json` reads the three configurations and the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed, and the configurations come solely from the arguments or files under the same validation, equality, pointer and key rules as `preview_config`. `decisions` is a JSON object, possibly empty, mapping original `preview_config` conflict paths to either the string `"target"`, the string `"current"` or a custom decision object; strings and custom objects may be mixed freely in the same map. Keys match verbatim using the same JSON Pointer escaping (`~0`, `~1`), with no trimming or Unicode normalization; only whole conflict paths are accepted — arrays, type changes and whole-object conflicts cannot be decided at subpaths, and non-conflict fields are rejected — and partial selections are allowed. Choosing `"target"` adopts that conflict's complete target-side presence state and value; choosing `"current"` keeps the current side and records the conflict as handled. When the chosen side is missing the field is deleted, and a `null` side value is kept as a value rather than treated as missing. Every other non-conflicting change and every independent current edit keeps its preview result.
24	
25	A custom decision object holds a strict boolean `present`. When `present` is true the object holds exactly `present` and a required `value`; when `present` is false it holds exactly `present` and the field is deleted. `value` accepts any legal JSON value, including `null`, arrays and objects. The custom value replaces the selected field wholesale: objects, arrays and type changes are never recursively merged, and a value numerically or structurally equal to the target or current side still counts as a custom, handled decision. Every other non-conflicting change and every independent current edit keeps its preview result. For example, when the port is 80 on the base side, 8080 on the target side and 9000 on the current side, a `{"present": true, "value": 9001}` decision on `/port` confirms 9001 while an independently modified timeout keeps its current value.
26	
27	The result holds only `baseVersion`, `targetVersion`, `canApply`, `config`, `conflicts` and `resolved`: `config` is the complete configuration after the choices, `conflicts` holds only the unchosen conflicts with their original details and current values, and `canApply` is true only when `conflicts` is empty. Each `resolved` entry holds only `path` and `choice`: `choice` is the confirmed string for side selections or `"custom"` for every custom selection. Both `conflicts` and `resolved` are sorted by path in Unicode code point order and are always present, even when empty. An invalid or unknown version, invalid store, a configuration violating the existing rules, a non-object decisions value, a non-string key, a key that is not an original conflict path, a choice that is neither a string nor an object, an illegal string choice, or a custom object with a missing field, an extra field, a non-boolean `present`, or a `value` containing a non-string key, a non-finite number, a non-JSON value or a circular reference raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the four files, printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid run prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when conflicts remain. Neither success nor failure modifies the arguments, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory, and mutating nested values in the returned result never reaches the passed inputs.
28

Both inputs follow the existing checklist and template rules, including the checklist version match and the at-least-one-required-item rule: the checklist must stay valid on its own even when, for example, every old item has become inapplicable. The template is filtered by the release's change categories exactly like `generate_checklist` — including the empty-selection and no-required-item errors — and items the filter would drop are still fully validated, as is the whole checklist and the whole store. Ids match case-sensitively after trimming surrounding whitespace, without Unicode normalization. When the normalized `text` and `required` of a same-id pair are both identical, the old status is kept even if the template moved the item, and the id is listed in `retained`; when either differs, the item takes the new definition with a uniform `pending` status and the id is listed in `reset`; applicable template items absent from the old checklist are added with `pending` status and their ids go in `added`; old items no longer applicable — whether filtered out by category or missing from the new template — are dropped and their ids follow the old checklist order into `removed`. The result holds only `version`, `items`, `retained`, `reset`, `added` and `removed`; `items` follows the applicable template order, each entry carrying only the normalized `id`, `text`, `required` and `status`, and the three change arrays follow template order while `removed` follows the old checklist order; every array is present even when empty. The output needs no required item to be `done` and can be passed straight to `checklist`/`check` or `audit_checklist`; template-declared status is ignored and status is never inferred from changed wording. An invalid version, unknown release, version mismatch, invalid checklist, template or store content, an empty filtered selection or a selection without any required item raises `ValueError`, and read failures raise `OSError`; the CLI reports these, plus non-UTF-8 or malformed JSON files and duplicate JSON object keys (whole-file rejection, as everywhere), as a single-line `error` object with exit 2, while success prints the single-line result with exit 0. A missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown, and no result ever modifies the store, the input files or the passed payloads, or creates any file or directory.
84	
85	`ReleaseDesk.reconcile_checklist_with_dependencies(version, checklist, template, base_dependencies, dependencies)` adds dependency-change progress alignment to that reconciliation, and `python3 release_desk.py reconcile-checklist 1.2.0 checklist.json template.json --base-dependencies base-dependencies.json --dependencies dependencies.json` reads the old and new dependency maps from two additional UTF-8 JSON files using the same positional arguments and `--store` selection; omitting both options keeps the original `reconcile-checklist` behavior exactly, and passing only one of them fails with a single-line `error` object and exit 2. The version, checklist, template and store rules follow `reconcile_checklist` unchanged. Both dependency values follow the existing dependency normalization rules: the old map is validated against the **whole old checklist** and the new map against the **whole new template** — including items no filter selects — so an illegal id, an unknown reference, a self dependency or a cycle anywhere in either graph fails.
86	
87	The final scope follows `generate_checklist_with_dependencies`: the new template is filtered by the release's change categories first — an empty initial filter or an initial selection without any required item still raises `ValueError` — then closed over every direct and indirect prerequisite of the selected items in the new graph, including prerequisites whose own categories do not apply. Items in the final scope that are absent from the old checklist enter `added` with a uniform `pending` status. An old item whose normalized `text`, `required` or direct prerequisite id set changed enters `reset` with `pending` status; prerequisite sets compare order-insensitively and a missing key means the empty set. Any other old item in the final scope that can reach an added or reset item along the new graph also enters `reset` and becomes `pending` — an existing prerequisite that is merely `pending` or `blocked` never triggers a reset by itself, and template-declared status is still ignored. Every remaining old item keeps its old status and enters `retained`.
88	
89	The result holds the six `reconcile_checklist` fields — `version`, `items`, `retained`, `reset`, `added` and `removed` — plus `dependencies` and `includedPrerequisites`. `items` carries the new definitions in new template order; `retained`, `reset` and `added` follow the same order, `removed` lists the old items outside the final scope in old checklist order, and the four classifications are mutually exclusive. `dependencies` covers every result id in template order with its normalized new-graph prerequisite array (dependency-array order preserved, a missing key frozen to `[]`), and `includedPrerequisites` lists, in template order, only the ids added solely because of a dependency edge; every array is always present. An invalid or unknown version, a version mismatch, invalid store, checklist, template or dependency content, a filter failure, non-UTF-8 bytes, a JSON syntax error or a repeated object key at any level raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI prints only a single-line `error` object with exit 2 for any of these and the single-line result JSON with exit 0 on success, a not-ready result included. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory, and mutating nested data in the returned result never reaches the passed inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.
90	
91	`ReleaseDesk.migrate_checklist(base_version, target_version, checklist, template)` is a read-only cross-version migration that lets a target-version checklist inherit only check progress still backed by evidence in the target release, and `python3 release_desk.py migrate-checklist 1.0.0 2.0.0 checklist.json template.json` reads the base checklist and target template from two UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first, then both versions are looked up); migrating a version to itself or migrating in reverse version order is allowed. The checklist follows the existing checklist rules and its declared version must equal the base version, while the template follows the existing template rules; the template is filtered by the **target** version's change categories exactly like `generate_checklist` — including the empty-selection and no-required-item errors — and template items the filter would drop are still fully validated, as is the whole checklist and the whole store.
92	
93	Item ids match case-sensitively after trimming surrounding whitespace, without Unicode normalization. A target template item without a same-id old item is added with uniform `pending` status; a same-id item whose normalized `text` or `required` differs is redefined and reset to `pending`. When the definition is identical, the two releases are compared with the same category classification, trimmed-text matching, order-insensitive pairing and duplicate-count rules as `diff` — a change in the order of entries alone never resets an item — scoped to the categories the **new template item** declares: an item declaring no `categories` compares all three categories, and a multi-category item compares every category it declares, categories absent from the target release included. Only when every compared category is completely unchanged (nothing added and nothing removed in that category) between the two releases is the old status kept and the id listed in `retained`; otherwise the item takes the new definition with `pending` status and the id is listed in `reset`. For example, when only the Added entries change a Fixed-scoped done item stays `done`, while losing one of two duplicate Fixed entries resets even the Fixed item. Old items that do not appear in the filtered target selection — whether filtered out because the target release no longer has any of their declared categories or missing from the new template — are removed, their ids following the old checklist order.
94	
95	The result holds only `baseVersion`, `version`, `items`, `retained`, `reset`, `added` and `removed`, where `version` is the target version; `items` follows the target template order and each entry carries only the normalized `id`, `text`, `required` and `status`, so the result can be passed straight to `checklist`/`check` or `audit_checklist` against the target version. `retained`, `reset` and `added` hold ids in target template order, `removed` holds ids in old checklist order, and all four arrays are present even when empty. Template-declared status is ignored and status is never inferred from change texts. An invalid or unknown version (base or target), invalid store, checklist or template content, a checklist version mismatch, an empty filtered selection or a selection without any required item raises `ValueError`, and read failures raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in either file, printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2 for any of these and the single-line result with exit 0 on success. A missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed payloads, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory, and mutating nested values in the returned result never reaches the passed inputs. The existing same-version rule of `reconcile_checklist` is unchanged.
96	
97	`ReleaseDesk.migrate_checklist_with_dependencies(base_version, target_version, checklist, template, base_dependencies, dependencies)` adds dependency-graph alignment to that cross-version migration, and `python3 release_desk.py migrate-checklist 1.0.0 2.0.0 checklist.json template.json --base-dependencies base-dependencies.json --dependencies dependencies.json` reads the old and new dependency maps from two additional UTF-8 JSON files using the same positional arguments and `--store` selection; omitting both options keeps the original `migrate-checklist` behavior exactly, and passing only one of them fails with a single-line `error` object and exit 2. The version, checklist, template and store rules follow `migrate_checklist` unchanged: both versions must be registered (same-version and reverse-order migrations allowed), the checklist declares the base version, and the whole store is validated before either version is looked up. Both dependency values follow the existing dependency normalization rules: the old map is validated against the **whole old checklist** and the new map against the **whole new template** — including items no filter selects — so an illegal id, an unknown reference, a self dependency or a cycle anywhere in either graph fails.
98	
99	The final scope follows `generate_checklist_with_dependencies`: the new template is filtered by the target release's change categories first — an empty initial filter or an initial selection without any required item still raises `ValueError` — then closed over every direct and indirect prerequisite of the selected items in the new graph, including prerequisites whose own categories do not apply; shared prerequisites are collected once. Items in the final scope that are absent from the old checklist enter `added` with a uniform `pending` status. An old item whose normalized `text`, `required` or direct prerequisite id set changed enters `reset` with `pending` status; prerequisite sets compare order-insensitively and a missing key means the empty set. When the definition and the prerequisite set are identical, the change-evidence comparison of `migrate_checklist` decides: the two releases are compared with the `diff` classification (trimmed-text matching, order-insensitive pairing, duplicate counts), scoped to the categories the new template item declares — no `categories` compares all three — and only when every compared category is completely unchanged is the old status kept and the id listed in `retained`; otherwise the id enters `reset`. Any other old item in the final scope that can reach an added or reset item along the new graph also enters `reset` and becomes `pending` — an existing prerequisite that is merely `pending` or `blocked` never triggers a reset by itself, and template-declared status is still ignored. Old items outside the final scope enter `removed` in old checklist order.
100	
101	The result holds the seven `migrate_checklist` fields — `baseVersion`, `version`, `items`, `retained`, `reset`, `added` and `removed` — plus `dependencies` and `includedPrerequisites`. `items` carries the new definitions in new template order, each entry holding only the normalized `id`, `text`, `required` and `status`; `retained`, `reset` and `added` follow the same order, `removed` follows the old checklist order, and the four classifications are mutually exclusive. `dependencies` covers every result id in template order with its normalized new-graph prerequisite array (dependency-array order preserved, a missing key frozen to `[]`), and `includedPrerequisites` lists, in template order, only the ids added solely because of a dependency edge; every array is always present. An invalid or unknown version, a checklist version mismatch, invalid store, checklist, template or dependency content, a filter failure, non-UTF-8 bytes, a JSON syntax error or a repeated object key at any level raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI prints only a single-line `error` object with exit 2 for any of these and the single-line result JSON with exit 0 on success. A missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory, and mutating nested data in the returned result never reaches the passed inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.
102	
103	`ReleaseDesk.update_checklist(version, updates, checklist_path)` applies a batch of status updates to a local checklist file, confirming each entry against the status currently stored, and `python3 release_desk.py update-checklist 1.2.0 updates.json checklist.json` reads the batch from a UTF-8 JSON file using the same `--store` selection and treats the third positional path as the write target. The version follows the existing version rules and must be registered (the whole store is validated first; a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown), and the target checklist follows the existing checklist rules, including the rule that its declared version must equal the queried version and its at-least-one-required-item rule.
104	
105	The updates value is an array, which may be empty; every entry holds exactly `id`, `expected` and `status` — a non-dict entry, a missing or extra field, or a structural root that is not an array is rejected. Ids follow the single-line checklist id rule (a trimmed, non-empty string with no carriage returns or newlines in the raw value), match case-sensitively after trimming surrounding whitespace with no Unicode normalization, and must be unique within the batch after normalization. `expected` and `status` must each be one of `done`, `pending` and `blocked`, and any status may switch to any other; a value that is already the target status is still checked. Every `expected` status is compared with the status read from the checklist, including entries whose target status would not change anything, and a single mismatch — or an id absent from the checklist — rejects the whole batch with `ValueError` before anything is written.
106	
107	The result holds only `version`, `changed`, `items`, `updated` and `ready`. `items` keeps the checklist order and the normalized four fields, changing only the statuses of matched items; `updated` is always an array and lists, in checklist order, only the ids whose status actually changed; `ready` follows the existing readiness rule of every required item being `done`. `changed` is true only when at least one status actually changes. When it is true the target is replaced wholesale with a UTF-8 JSON object holding only `version` and `items`, ending in a newline; when it is false the target's bytes and modification time are left completely untouched. An empty batch is a valid run that still validates the version, the store and the whole checklist, changing nothing.
108	
109	The target file must already exist and must not be a symbolic link, and it must not be the same file as the store or, on the CLI, as the updates file — textual path aliases and hard links are recognized — with violations raising `ValueError`; a missing target and any read or write failure raise `OSError`, and neither a missing target nor missing directories are ever created. An invalid version, an unknown release, an invalid checklist or store, an illegal update structure or id, a duplicate or unknown update id, an expected-status mismatch, non-UTF-8 bytes, a JSON syntax error or a repeated object key at any level raises `ValueError`. Any failure preserves the target's original bytes and never creates a file or directory, and success or failure never modifies the updates array, the updates file or the store. The CLI prints the single-line result with exit 0 on success and a single-line `error` object with exit 2 on failure.
110	
111	`ReleaseDesk.preview_update_checklist(version, updates, checklist_path)` is a read-only dry run of the same batch: it confirms whether the whole batch would be accepted and shows the planned checklist and readiness without writing, and `python3 release_desk.py update-checklist 1.2.0 updates.json checklist.json --dry-run` runs it with the same positional arguments and `--store` selection; omitting the flag keeps the original writing behavior exactly. The preview follows the same public version, store, checklist, update-entry and id-matching rules as `update_checklist`, in the same order — the version must be registered after the whole store is validated (a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown), the target must already exist, must not be a symbolic link and must not alias the store or, on the CLI, the updates file (textual aliases and hard links recognized), and non-UTF-8 bytes, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level are rejected. An empty updates array is a valid preview that still validates the whole store and the whole checklist. Illegal input, an unregistered version, a checklist version mismatch, an invalid store, non-UTF-8 bytes, a JSON syntax error or a repeated key raises `ValueError`; a read failure or a missing target raises `OSError`; neither success nor failure modifies the passed array, the updates file, the checklist file, its modification time or the store, and no file or directory is created.
112	
113	Instead of raising, unknown ids and expected-status mismatches become conflict entries reported in updates-array order: each conflict holds only the normalized `id`, the `expected` status, `actual`, the target `status` and `reason`; `actual` is `null` with reason `unknown-id` for an id absent from the checklist, and `reason` is `status-mismatch` with the read status as `actual` otherwise. A target status that is already satisfied still has its `expected` status checked. The result holds only `version`, `canUpdate`, `changed`, `items`, `updated`, `ready` and `conflicts`, and every array is always present. With no conflicts `canUpdate` is true, `items` keeps the checklist order and normalized four fields changing only matched statuses, `updated` lists, in checklist order, only the ids whose status would actually change, and `changed` is true only when that array is non-empty; `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. With any conflict `canUpdate` is false, `items` is the normalized original checklist unchanged, `updated` is empty, `changed` is false and no partial update is reported; `ready` then reflects the original checklist. A valid preview prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when it reports conflicts; any exception prints only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. Other public entry points keep their existing behavior.
114	
115	`ReleaseDesk.preview_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, current)` is a read-only three-way merge preview of same-version checklists, and `python3 release_desk.py merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json current.json` reads the common base, the incoming checklist and the current checklist from three UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection. All three inputs follow the existing checklist rules — including the rule that each declared version must equal the queried version — the whole store is validated before the version is looked up (a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown), and the version must be registered. Items are matched by their normalized ids, case-sensitively after trimming with no Unicode normalization, and compared as whole normalized items: only `id`, `text`, `required` and `status` take part, extra fields are ignored, and a missing item differs from any present one.
116	
117	For each id, an incoming side equal to the base or to the current side keeps the current side; otherwise a current side equal to the base adopts the incoming side; every remaining case is one whole-item conflict that keeps the current side's presence state and content. Additions, deletions and modifications all follow this rule, non-conflicting changes still enter the preview, and item fields are never merged separately. The result holds only `version`, `canMerge`, `ready`, `items` and `conflicts`: `canMerge` is true only when no conflict was reported, and `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. `items` carries only the four normalized fields, keeps the current-side item order and then appends, in incoming-side order, the preview items the current side lacks. `conflicts` is always an array, sorted by id in Unicode code point order, each entry holding only `id`, `base`, `incoming` and `current`, the last three being the complete normalized item or `null` when that side lacks the id. A preview that would be empty or would hold no required item raises `ValueError`, and this result validation applies to conflicting previews too.
118	
119	An invalid or unregistered version, a declared-version mismatch, an invalid checklist or store, an empty preview or a preview without any required item raises `ValueError`, while a missing or unreadable file raises `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the three files, printing only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid preview — conflicts included — prints the single-line result with exit 0. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed payloads, the input files or the store, no file or directory is created, and mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. Other public entry points keep their existing behavior.
120	
121	`ReleaseDesk.resolve_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, current, decisions)` is a read-only confirmation layer over `preview_merge_checklist`, and `python3 release_desk.py resolve-merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json current.json decisions.json` reads the three checklists and the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection. The version, checklist, store and version-registration checks follow `merge-checklist` exactly, including validating the whole store first, treating a missing store as empty and then reporting the version as unknown, matching declared versions, comparing whole normalized items, merging non-conflicting changes identically, and requiring both the original preview and the confirmed checklist to be non-empty and to contain at least one required item.
122	
123	`decisions` is a JSON object, possibly empty, mapping original preview conflict ids to the string `"incoming"`, the string `"current"` or a custom decision object; partial selections are allowed and strings and custom objects may be mixed freely. Keys match the normalized conflict ids exactly — case-sensitively, without trimming surrounding whitespace or Unicode normalization — and a key that is not an original conflict id is rejected, as is any non-object decision value, non-string key or choice that is neither one of the two strings nor a well-formed custom object. Choosing a side adopts that side's complete item; item fields are never merged separately. When the chosen side lacks the id the item is deleted, and choosing a side whose content is unchanged still counts as a confirmed decision. Unchosen conflicts keep their original details (including the current side's presence state and content) and keep the current item in the checklist; their fields are never merged field by field.
124	
125	A custom decision object holds a strict boolean `present` and nothing else beyond an optional `value`. When `present` is true the object holds exactly `present` and `value`, and `value` is a whole checklist item holding exactly `id`, `text`, `required` and `status`, each validated and trimmed with the usual checklist field rules; the normalized item id must equal the decision key. The custom item replaces the conflicted item wholesale — fields are never merged separately — even when it is identical to one of the sides. When `present` is false the object holds exactly `present` and the item is deleted, even when the current side already lacks it. Either way the decision is recorded in `resolved` with the choice `"custom"`. A malformed custom object — a non-boolean `present`, missing or extra fields, an invalid item or an id that does not match the decision key — raises `ValueError`.
126	
127	The result holds only `version`, `canMerge`, `ready`, `items`, `conflicts` and `resolved`. `items` carries only the four normalized fields, follows the current-side item order and then appends, in incoming-side order, items the current side originally lacked; confirmed deletions are absent. `canMerge` is true only when `conflicts` is empty, and `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. `conflicts` holds only the unconfirmed conflicts in the preview structure, and each `resolved` entry holds only `id` and the confirmed choice — `incoming`, `current` or `custom`. Both arrays are always present and are sorted by id in Unicode code point order. An invalid or unregistered version, a declared-version mismatch, an invalid checklist or store, a non-object decisions value, a non-string key, a key that is not an original conflict id, an illegal choice or malformed custom decision, or an empty or required-item-free original preview or confirmed checklist raises `ValueError`, while a missing or unreadable checklist or decisions file raises `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the four files, printing only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid run prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when conflicts remain. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store, no file or directory is created, and mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.
128	
129	`ReleaseDesk.apply_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, expected, decisions, current_path)` saves a confirmed merge to a local checklist file, and `python3 release_desk.py apply-merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json expected.json decisions.json current.json` reads the base, incoming and expected checklists plus the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection and treats the fifth path as the write target. The version, checklist, decisions, store and version-registration checks follow `resolve-merge-checklist` exactly, with the expected checklist validated like every other checklist. The target file must already exist and must not be a symbolic link, and it must not be the same file as the store or as any of the four input files — textual path aliases and hard links are recognized — with violations raising `ValueError`; a missing target or any read or write failure raises `OSError`, and neither a missing target nor missing directories are ever created. The file is read as UTF-8 JSON under the same whole-file duplicate-key rule as everywhere (encoding, syntax and repeated-key errors raise `ValueError`), validated like any checklist, and its declared version and normalized item sequence must equal the expected snapshot: extra fields, object key order and trimmable surrounding whitespace do not take part, item order does, and any mismatch raises `ValueError` before anything is written. The merge then follows `resolve_merge_checklist` exactly — whole-item merging, incoming/current side selections, custom replacements and deletions, ordering and result legality — with the actually read target as the current side; any conflict left undecided raises `ValueError`, an empty decisions object is valid when there are no conflicts, and a not-ready result still saves. The result holds only `version`, `changed`, `items`, `resolved` and `ready`, where `items` and `resolved` carry the same content and ordering as the corresponding `resolve_merge_checklist` result. `changed` is true only when the normalized item sequence differs from the read one; then the target is replaced wholesale with UTF-8 JSON holding only `version` and `items` and ending in a newline, and when it is false the target's bytes and modification time are left untouched. Validation and read or write failures always preserve the target's original bytes and leave no new file or directory behind, and neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store; mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.

# Release Desk

Maintain local release records and generate Markdown notes grouped as Added, Changed and Fixed. Requires Python 3.10+; only the standard library is used.

`python3 release_desk.py notes 1.1.0` renders the included second release. `python3 release_desk.py versions` lists sample versions in numeric order. `samples/next-changes.json` is a candidate change list; to try registration without changing the sample store, use `python3 release_desk.py --store .state/releases.json add 1.2.0 samples/next-changes.json` and query that same store.

Version identifiers have exactly three nonnegative numeric components, without prefixes, prerelease suffixes or leading zeros. Each release has at least one single-line change with a recognized category. Existing versions cannot be replaced. Category order is fixed and the input order within a category is retained. This version does not inspect Git or publish packages.

`python3 release_desk.py diff 1.0.0 1.1.0` compares two registered versions in the same store and prints a single-line JSON object with `baseVersion`, `targetVersion` and the `added`, `removed` and `unchanged` entries of the target relative to the base. Entries match on category plus trimmed, case-sensitive text; duplicates pair up by occurrence. Comparing a version with itself or a higher with a lower version is allowed. The comparison is read-only and never infers actual product changes.

`ReleaseDesk.diff_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config)` is a read-only structural comparison of two externally supplied JSON configuration objects, and `python3 release_desk.py diff-config 1.0.0 1.1.0 base.json target.json` reads both configurations from UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); comparing a version with itself or a higher with a lower version is allowed. The configurations come solely from the arguments or files — they are never written to the store and never inferred from change entries — and neither the passed objects, the files nor the store are modified, and no directory is created.

Each root configuration must be a JSON object. When the same field exists in both and both values are objects, comparison descends recursively; otherwise the complete values are compared. Arrays are never split: they compare as whole values and element order is significant, with objects inside arrays following the same object rules. A field or whole subobject present only in the target yields one `added` entry, one present only in the base yields one `removed` entry, both carrying `path` and `value`; a field present on both sides with differing values yields a `changed` entry carrying `path`, `before` (the base value) and `after` (the target value). All three arrays are always present, and identical configurations return three empty arrays. `path` is a JSON Pointer rooted at the empty string (`/a/b`, `/` for an empty field name), with `~` and `/` in field names escaped as `~0` and `~1`. Each array is sorted by path in Unicode code point order; key matching is case-sensitive with no Unicode normalization and empty key names are allowed. Booleans differ from numbers even when comparing `true` with `1`, numerically equal integers and floats compare equal, `null` differs from a missing field, and object key order is ignored.

An invalid or unknown version, invalid store content, a non-object root, a non-string key, a non-JSON value (including non-finite numbers) or a circular reference raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects encoding errors, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level (the same whole-file duplicate-key rule as everywhere), printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2 for any of these and the single-line result with exit 0 on success. A missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown.

`ReleaseDesk.preview_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config)` is a read-only three-way preview that checks whether applying the base→target plan would overwrite independent edits already present in the current configuration, and `python3 release_desk.py preview-config 1.0.0 2.0.0 base.json target.json current.json` reads all three configurations from UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed, just like `diff-config`. The configurations come solely from the arguments or files and follow the same validation, equality, pointer and key rules as `diff_config`, and nothing — the passed objects, the files, the store — is modified and no directory is created.

For each field, the plan is the base→target change. A field the plan does not change keeps its current presence state and value, including independent current edits and current-only fields.     def migrate_checklist_with_dependencies(self, base_version, target_version, checklist,
                                            template, base_dependencies, dependencies):
        # Read-only cross-version migration that additionally aligns the
        # dependency graphs: the new template is filtered by the target
        # release's change categories and closed over every direct and
        # indirect prerequisite exactly like
        # generate_checklist_with_dependencies, then progress is migrated
        # like migrate_checklist with the dependency graph as an additional
        # reset condition and reset propagation along the new graph. The old
        # graph is validated against the whole old checklist and the new
        # graph against the whole new template, items no filter selects
        # included. Nothing is written and the passed objects are never
        # mutated.
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        # The checklist is validated against the base version it declares; the
        # template is validated in full before the target filter is applied.
        items = self._validated_checklist(checklist, base_version)
        template_items = self._validated_template(template)
        # Every id in either dependency map, at either end, must reference an
        # item of its own side: the old map is checked against the complete
        # old checklist, the new map against the complete new template.
        base_prerequisites = self._validated_dependencies(
            base_dependencies, {item["id"] for item in items})
        prerequisites = self._validated_dependencies(
            dependencies, {item["id"] for item in template_items})
        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
        records = self._read_store()
        if base_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        if target_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        selected = self._applicable_template_items(template_items, records[target_version])
        selected_ids = {item["id"] for item in selected}
        # Close over every direct and indirect prerequisite of the selected
        # items; shared prerequisites are collected once. Only the member set
        # matters here: the final order always follows the template.
        closure = set(selected_ids)
        pending = list(selected_ids)
        while pending:
            node = pending.pop()
            for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(node, ()):
                if prerequisite not in closure:
                    closure.add(prerequisite)
                    pending.append(prerequisite)
        selected_by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in selected}
        # The expected definition of every final id, in template order, with
        # the uniform pending shape of dependency-generated checklists.
        expected_items = []
        for item in template_items:
            item_id = item["id"]
            if item_id not in closure:
                continue
            if item_id in selected_ids:
                expected_items.append(dict(selected_by_id[item_id]))
            else:
                expected_items.append({"id": item_id, "text": item["text"],
                                       "required": item["required"], "status": "pending"})
        # Reuse the diff classification as the change comparison; the scope
        # filters it down to the categories a template item declares. When the
        # item declares none every category is compared, categories not present
        # in the target release included.
        added, removed, unchanged = self._diff_entries(
            self._clean_changes(records[base_version]),
            self._clean_changes(records[target_version]))
        changed_by_category = {}
        for category in CATEGORIES:
            changed_by_category[category] = any(
                entry["category"] == category for entry in added + removed)
        # Ids match case-sensitively after trimming, without Unicode normalization.
        previous = {item["id"]: item for item in items}
        definitions = {item["id"]: item for item in template_items}
        classification = {}
        for expected in expected_items:
            item_id = expected["id"]
            actual = previous.get(item_id)
            if actual is None:
                classification[item_id] = "added"
                continue
            # A redefined item returns to pending; the direct prerequisite
            # id set is part of the definition, compared order-insensitively
            # with a missing key meaning the empty set.
            old_prerequisites = set(base_prerequisites.get(item_id, ()))
            new_prerequisites = set(prerequisites.get(item_id, ()))
            if (actual["text"] != expected["text"]
                    or actual["required"] != expected["required"]
                    or old_prerequisites != new_prerequisites):
                classification[item_id] = "reset"
                continue
            categories = definitions[item_id]["categories"]
            scope = CATEGORIES if categories is None else tuple(categories)
            if all(not changed_by_category[category] for category in scope):
                classification[item_id] = "retained"
            else:
                classification[item_id] = "reset"
        # Any old item in the final scope that can reach an added or reset
        # item along the new graph is reset as well; an existing prerequisite
        # that is merely pending or blocked never triggers a reset by itself.
        # Reverse reachability from the initial triggers is already the fixed
        # point: anything reaching a propagated reset also reaches a trigger.
        triggers = {item_id for item_id, kind in classification.items()
                    if kind in ("added", "reset")}
        dependents = {}
        for node, node_prerequisites in prerequisites.items():
            for prerequisite in node_prerequisites:
                dependents.setdefault(prerequisite, []).append(node)
        reached = set()
        stack = list(triggers)
        while stack:
            node = stack.pop()
            for dependent in dependents.get(node, ()):
                if dependent not in triggers and dependent not in reached:
                    reached.add(dependent)
                    stack.append(dependent)
        for item_id in reached:
            if classification.get(item_id) == "retained":
                classification[item_id] = "reset"
        migrated, retained, reset, added_ids = [], [], [], []
        for expected in expected_items:
            item_id = expected["id"]
            kind = classification[item_id]
            if kind == "retained":
                migrated.append({"id": item_id, "text": expected["text"],
                                 "required": expected["required"],
                                 "status": previous[item_id]["status"]})
                retained.append(item_id)
            else:
                migrated.append({"id": item_id, "text": expected["text"],
                                 "required": expected["required"], "status": "pending"})
                (added_ids if kind == "added" else reset).append(item_id)
        removed_ids = [item["id"] for item in items if item["id"] not in closure]
        # Every final id gets a normalized array in template order; omitted
        # items and declared empty arrays both freeze to [].
        dependency_pairs = [(item["id"], list(prerequisites.get(item["id"], ())))
                            for item in expected_items]
        # includedPrerequisites lists, in template order, only the items
        # added solely because of a dependency edge.
        included_prerequisites = [item["id"] for item in expected_items
                                  if item["id"] not in selected_ids]
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "version": target_version,
                "items": migrated,
                "retained": retained, "reset": reset, "added": added_ids,
                "removed": removed_ids,
                "dependencies": dict(dependency_pairs),
                "includedPrerequisites": included_prerequisites}

    def update_checklist(self, version, updates, checklist_path):
        # Batch-update the statuses of a local checklist file after confirming
        # every expected status still matches the read bytes: one mismatch
        # rejects the whole batch. Only when at least one status changes is the
        # target replaced wholesale with UTF-8 JSON ending in a newline;
        # otherwise its bytes and modification time are left untouched.
        normalized_updates, items, path = self._prepare_checklist_update(
            version, updates, checklist_path)
        status_by_id = {item["id"]: item["status"] for item in items}
        # Ids match case-sensitively after trimming, without Unicode
        # normalization; every expected status is checked, including entries
        # whose target status would not change anything.
        for item_id, expected, _status in normalized_updates:
            actual = status_by_id.get(item_id)
            if actual is None:
                raise ValueError("update item id must exist in the checklist")
            if actual != expected:
                raise ValueError("update expected status does not match the checklist")
        updated, resulting = self._apply_checklist_updates(items, normalized_updates)
        changed = bool(updated)
        if changed:
            content = json.dumps({"version": version, "items": resulting},
                                 ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
            _atomic_write(path, content)
        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in resulting if item["required"])
        return {"version": version, "changed": changed, "items": resulting,
                "updated": updated, "ready": ready}

    def preview_update_checklist(self, version, updates, checklist_path):
        # Read-only plan for update_checklist: the same public validation,
        # store and checklist checks and the same id matching, but unknown ids
        # and expected-status mismatches are reported as conflicts in updates
        # order instead of raised, and nothing is ever written.
        normalized_updates, items, _path = self._prepare_checklist_update(
            version, updates, checklist_path)
        status_by_id = {item["id"]: item["status"] for item in items}
        # Every expected status is checked, including entries whose target
        # status is already satisfied; conflicts keep the updates-array order.
        conflicts = []
        for item_id, expected, target in normalized_updates:
            actual = status_by_id.get(item_id)
            if actual is None:
                conflicts.append({"id": item_id, "expected": expected, "actual": None,
                                  "status": target, "reason": "unknown-id"})
            elif actual != expected:
                conflicts.append({"id": item_id, "expected": expected, "actual": actual,
                                  "status": target, "reason": "status-mismatch"})
        if conflicts:
            # A conflicting batch plans nothing: the normalized original
            # checklist is reported without any partial status changes.
            can_update = False
            resulting = [dict(item) for item in items]
            updated = []
            changed = False
        else:
            can_update = True
            updated, resulting = self._apply_checklist_updates(items, normalized_updates)
            changed = bool(updated)
        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in resulting if item["required"])
        return {"version": version, "canUpdate": can_update, "changed": changed,
                "items": resulting, "updated": updated, "ready": ready,
                "conflicts": conflicts}

    def preview_merge_checklist(self, version, base, incoming, current):
        # Read-only three-way merge preview of same-version checklists: items
        # are matched by normalized id and compared as whole normalized items
        # (id, text, required, status; extra fields ignored, missing differing
        # from any present item). An incoming side equal to the base or to the
        # current side keeps the current side; otherwise a current side equal
        # to the base adopts the incoming side; anything else is one whole-item
        # conflict that keeps the current presence state and content.
        base_items, incoming_items, current_items = self._prepared_merge_inputs(
            version, base, incoming, current)
        merged, conflicts = self._merge_classification(
            base_items, incoming_items, current_items)
        items = self._ordered_merge_items(merged, incoming_items, current_items)
        self._validate_merge_items(items)
        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in items if item["required"])

        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):

        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        base_items = self._validated_checklist(base, version)
        incoming_items = self._validated_checklist(incoming, version)
        current_items = self._validated_checklist(current, version)
